editorial.headline: Public Opinion Polling: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Research into public views and voting behaviour is open nationally to full foreign ownership, but PMA registration is blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
Public-opinion polling is a research activity concerned with how people describe their lives, choices and public orientation. The stated scope covers studies of quality of life and lifestyle; social and political participants; party preference; and voting behaviour. It is consequently defined by investigation of opinion across both everyday and political questions. These subjects sit within one activity: research into the views people hold and the choices they make, from lifestyle questions through to participation, party preference and voting.

Registration is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. The record therefore makes the activity available at each of the four listed business scales. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to PMA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no national foreign-share limitation below full ownership in the supplied record. That national position is supported by Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a foreign-owned company considering this activity nationally, the position is direct: it is open to PMA registration with up to full foreign ownership.

That national openness is not the answer for PMA registration in Bali. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s relevant prohibition. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. This is not a lower Bali foreign-ownership ceiling; it is a block on PMA registration arising from the local risk-class moratorium, notwithstanding the national 100% ceiling.

The distinction is decisive. The 100% ceiling describes the national foreign-ownership position; it does not override Bali’s permanent risk-class moratorium. The record’s Bali outcome follows the local rule that blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. Thus, while the activity remains nationally open at the listed scales, the current Bali conclusion for a PMA applicant is unequivocal: registration is blocked. That is the operative Bali result for this activity, based on its stated risk treatment and the provincial moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness permits full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-class moratorium blocks PMA registration for this activity.
